relationship_to_prior.new_question: Estimate trait-axis and family-axis repeatability separately; do not classify which axis dominates.
relationship_to_prior.independence_rule: The previous log variance-ratio precision failure is retained and cannot be overwritten by this study.

biological_question: How much of the variation in phylogenetic memory-loss rate is repeatable across lineages for the same trait, and how much is repeatable across traits within the same lineage?

response.effect: all-pair Spearman(patristic separation, absolute species-state difference)

interpretation.R_trait: cross-lineage portability of trait-specific phylogenetic memory
interpretation.R_family: cross-trait repeatability of lineage-level evolutionary memory regime
interpretation.R_residual: family-by-trait specificity plus measurement/model residual; no mechanistic decomposition claimed

model.hard_rule: Do not label one axis dominant or test R_trait > R_family in this version.

model_informativeness.benchmark_source: Reuse the exact three pre-outcome known-truth parameter sets from data/trait_memory_model_informativeness_v0_6_1.json.
model_informativeness.failure_rule: If any benchmark fails any criterion, stop before opening real memory rho. Do not change the core, model, benchmark, or error tolerance.

real_analysis_if_admitted.intervals: 2.5% and 97.5% percentile intervals for each repeatability share
real_analysis_if_admitted.prune_only: same model and identical system set using prune-only rho
real_analysis_if_admitted.leave_one_out: pre-frozen leave-one-trait and leave-one-family descriptive robustness

hard_nonclaims: No claim that trait repeatability exceeds family repeatability or vice versa.
No mechanistic interpretation of the residual component.
No outcome-driven removal of families or traits.
No new data source or threshold relaxation.
